title.en: When the Power Came Back On

synopsis: A neighborhood blackout reveals the lives behind the doors of one apartment building.
grammarFocus: Past contrasts · imperfect, preterite and reported speech
coverImagePrompt: Old Buenos Aires apartment courtyard during night power outage, candlelight glowing balconies neighbors talking

sentences.es: A las nueve y cuarto, todas las luces del edificio se apagaron al mismo tiempo.
sentences.en: At nine fifteen, every light in the building went out at once.

sentences.es: Sofía estaba preparando una presentación para el trabajo cuando su computadora dejó de funcionar.
sentences.en: Sofía was preparing a presentation for work when her computer stopped working.

annotations.explanation: Estar in the imperfect with a gerund presents an action in progress when another event interrupted.

examples.es: Estaba preparando la cena cuando llamaste.
examples.en: I was making dinner when you called.

examples.es: Ellos estaban trabajando cuando empezó a llover.
examples.en: They were working when it started to rain.

sentences.es: Durante unos segundos esperó a que regresara la electricidad, pero la pantalla permaneció oscura.
sentences.en: For a few seconds she waited for the power to come back, but the screen stayed dark.

annotations.explanation: Esperar a que often takes the subjunctive when the awaited event is uncertain.

sentences.es: Desde la calle llegaban bocinas, voces y el ruido de un autobús que no podía avanzar.
sentences.en: From the street came car horns, voices, and the noise of a bus that could not move forward.

sentences.es: Sofía salió al pasillo con la linterna del teléfono y encontró a su vecino del tercero sentado en las escaleras.
sentences.en: Sofía went into the hallway with her phone flashlight and found her third-floor neighbor sitting on the stairs.

sentences.es: Se llamaba Julián y vivía allí desde hacía ocho años, aunque apenas se habían saludado.
sentences.en: His name was Julián, and he had lived there for eight years, although they had barely greeted one another.

annotations.explanation: Desde hacía describes how long something had already been true at a point in the past.

sentences.es: «El ascensor no funciona y mi madre está arriba», explicó, señalando el quinto piso.
sentences.en: “The elevator isn’t working, and my mother is upstairs,” he explained, pointing to the fifth floor.

sentences.es: Sofía se ofreció a acompañarlo, y subieron despacio para no tropezar con los escalones.
sentences.en: Sofía offered to go with him, and they climbed slowly so they would not trip on the steps.

annotations.explanation: Para + infinitive expresses purpose; the no comes before the infinitive.

sentences.es: En el cuarto piso encontraron a una niña que sostenía una vela y buscaba a su gato.
sentences.en: On the fourth floor they found a girl holding a candle and looking for her cat.

sentences.es: Los tres escucharon un maullido detrás de una puerta y descubrieron al animal escondido entre unas cajas.
sentences.en: The three of them heard a meow behind a door and discovered the animal hiding among some boxes.

sentences.es: Cuando llegaron al quinto, la madre de Julián ya había preparado té con el agua caliente que quedaba en una tetera.
sentences.en: When they reached the fifth floor, Julián’s mother had already made tea with the hot water left in a kettle.

annotations.explanation: The pluperfect tells us the tea was prepared before they arrived.

sentences.es: Los invitó a entrar, y pronto aparecieron otros vecinos con galletas, velas y noticias del barrio.
sentences.en: She invited them in, and soon other neighbors appeared with cookies, candles, and neighborhood news.

sentences.es: Una arquitecta contó que el apagón afectaba a varias calles; un estudiante ofreció compartir su radio de pilas.
sentences.en: An architect said the blackout was affecting several streets; a student offered to share his battery-powered radio.

sentences.es: Al principio todos hablaban del problema, pero después empezaron a hablar de ellos mismos.
sentences.en: At first everyone talked about the problem, but later they began talking about themselves.

sentences.es: Sofía descubrió que Julián tocaba el violín, que la arquitecta había vivido en Lima y que la niña escribía historias de detectives.
sentences.en: Sofía discovered that Julián played the violin, the architect had lived in Lima, and the girl wrote detective stories.

sentences.es: Nadie miraba una pantalla y, sin embargo, la conversación parecía avanzar más rápido que cualquier mensaje.
sentences.en: Nobody was looking at a screen, and yet the conversation seemed to move faster than any message.

annotations.explanation: A connector that introduces a contrast between what came before and what follows.

sentences.es: A las once volvió la electricidad y las lámparas se encendieron, una detrás de otra.
sentences.en: At eleven the electricity returned, and the lamps came on, one after another.

sentences.es: Los vecinos guardaron sus cosas y se despidieron, pero nadie se apresuró a cerrar la puerta.
sentences.en: The neighbors put away their things and said goodbye, but nobody hurried to close the door.

sentences.es: A la mañana siguiente, Sofía bajó por las escaleras en lugar de tomar el ascensor.
sentences.en: The following morning, Sofía went down the stairs instead of taking the elevator.

annotations.explanation: En lugar de followed by an infinitive introduces an alternative action.

sentences.es: En el segundo piso se cruzó con Julián, que llevaba un pequeño cartel escrito a mano.
sentences.en: On the second floor she ran into Julián, who was carrying a small handwritten sign.

sentences.es: Decía: «Viernes, ocho de la noche: té en la azotea. No hace falta que se vaya la luz».
sentences.en: It said: “Friday, eight in the evening: tea on the rooftop. The power doesn’t have to go out.”

annotations.explanation: With a new subject, hacer falta que leads to a subjunctive verb.

sentences.es: Sofía sonrió, cambió el rumbo y fue a comprar galletas para el viernes.
sentences.en: Sofía smiled, changed direction, and went to buy cookies for Friday.

comprehension.question: Why do Sofía and Julián go upstairs?
comprehension.explanation: Julián’s mother is on the fifth floor, and the elevator is not working.

comprehension.question: What happens when the neighbors gather?
options: They begin to get to know one another
comprehension.explanation: Their conversation shifts from the blackout to their lives.

comprehension.question: What does Julián’s sign announce?
comprehension.explanation: It invites neighbors to tea on Friday, even without a blackout.
